summary: The test layer for the persistent-keyboard feature is strong, meaningful, and correctly balanced. Every one of the 13 user-spec acceptance criteria maps to at least one concrete test, and all the load-bearing assertions are behavioral rather than mock-only: the engine slow-lane ITs parse the recorded /sendMessage body as a JsonNode and assert the exact reply_markup shape (object-form keyboard rows in order, is_persistent, hardcoded resize_keyboard:true, one_time_keyboard, remove_keyboard:true) with the NON-default booleans seeded so a builder that ignored the step fields fails loudly; the executor unit tests capture the markup Map argument (not just verify(sender)); the controller IT round-trips ALL keyboard fields through PUT->response AND GET; copyOf is pinned for scalars, new-list-instance identity (assertNotSame) and copy-mutation isolation; and the no-v-html source guard in the preview spec still scans the real component source after stripping comments. The four cited 'covered by existing tests, not rewritten' claims (two re-enter-guard cases, keyword dispatch, menu precedence) are all real, assert the cited semantics, and are enabled. Findings are confined to minor/info: one real coverage gap (no test pins the duplicate-button trim semantics that case is NOT folded, Decision 6) and a handful of by-design notes. None blocking.

findings.title: Duplicate-button validation does not pin the case-NOT-folded semantics
findings.issue: Decision 6 states the duplicate-button check trims but does NOT fold case (HashSet on the trimmed raw text, unlike a lowercased keyword match). The test comment explicitly says 'case is NOT folded — Decision 6', but the only duplicate test asserts the TRIM path ('Бонус' vs ' Бонус '). There is no positive case proving that two labels differing only by case (e.g. 'Бонус' and 'бонус') are ACCEPTED. A future regression that lowercased the dedup key would silently start rejecting case-distinct labels and no test would catch it. The form mirror (FunnelStepForm.keyboard) has the same shape — only the trimmed-equal duplicate is tested, not the case-distinct accept.
findings.recommendation: Add a positive case to FunnelServiceKeyboardStepTest (and optionally the form spec): setKeyboard_caseDistinctButtonTexts_areAccepted — a SET_KEYBOARD with rows [['Бонус'],['бонос'? no — 'бонус']] updates without 422 and round-trips both labels. Cheap, directly pins the documented Decision-6 contract that distinguishes this dedup from the keyword contains-match.

findings.title: Engine IT does not assert keyboardText variable substitution on the wire (only literal text)
findings.issue: The slow-lane wire-body tests seed a literal keyboardText ('Choose:' / 'Keyboard removed.') and assert it verbatim in body.text. Variable substitution on the keyboard text path IS covered at the unit level (FunnelStepExecutorTest::setKeyboard_rendersVariablesAndParseMode) and at the controller-preview level (previewSetKeyboard...'Привіт Олена!'), so the full sweep->renderer->wire chain with a {user.*} variable substituted into the SENT body is not pinned by any single test. Low risk because each leg is independently covered, but a regression where the engine path skipped the renderer for keyboard steps (while the executor unit + preview kept working) would not be caught by an IT.
findings.recommendation: Optional: seed keyboardText with '{user.first_name}' in setKeyboardStep_sends... and assert body.text equals the substituted value for the seeded subscriber. Marginal — the executor unit already proves the executor renders; this would only add the full-engine integration of that path. Defer-acceptable.

findings.title: FunnelServiceKeyboardStepTest is an IT (extends AbstractIntegrationTest), not a pure unit test
findings.issue: The tech-spec Testing Strategy lists validateSetKeyboard/validateClearKeyboard under Unit tests, but the implemented test drives validation through FunnelService.update against real Mongo (AbstractIntegrationTest seed of user/project/funnel repos), cloning the FunnelServiceEmitEventTest pattern. It runs in the DEFAULT lane (no @Tag('slow')) so it is exercised on every push, and the round-trip-through-persist actually STRENGTHENS the toSteps/toStepDto coverage. Not a defect — just a pyramid classification note: this is integration-level coverage of unit-level logic, which is acceptable here because the validation is inseparable from the DTO mapping it guards.
findings.recommendation: None — accepted as designed. The choice mirrors the established FunnelServiceEmitEventTest precedent and adds persistence round-trip value.

findings.title: Preview clamp (>10 rows / >4 buttons / label>64) covered; clamp boundary pinned
findings.issue: The task Edge-cases section asked to confirm a test covers the Decision-7 clamp (preview echoes CLAMPED rows). It is covered: previewSetKeyboardClampsOversizedRows asserts 12-row/6-button/65-char input clamps to 10 rows x 4 buttons x 64-char label, and previewSetKeyboardLabelAtCapNotTruncated pins the 64-char inclusive boundary as NOT truncated. No gap.

findings.title: No-v-html source guard intact and not weakened by the keyboard branch
findings.issue: The guard reads the real FunnelMessagePreview.vue source via readFileSync, strips HTML/line/block comments, then asserts the source matches neither /v-html\s*=/ nor /.innerHTML\s*=/. It was NOT whitelisted or relaxed when the keyboard render branch was added; the keyboard branch additionally has runtime literal-text assertions (hostile label/text surface as text, no img/b elements created). Source guard confirmed intact.

findings.title: Assertion quality is high — no mock-only / tautology / over-mock failures found
findings.issue: Spot-checked every anti-pattern the task flagged. Wire-body cases parse the recorded /sendMessage JSON (OBJECT_MAPPER.readTree) and assert reply_markup structure, not request counts/HTTP 200. Executor cases use ArgumentCaptor<Object> on the markup arg and cast to Map (rows order, object-form {text:...}, hardcoded resize true) — never bare verify(sender). Round-trip asserts every keyboard field after BOTH PUT response and GET (toStepDto). copyOf asserts assertNotSame on the rows list AND copy-mutation isolation. Validation is double-covered with negatives (>64, duplicate, CLEAR-rejects-rows). Form specs assert the emitted payload shape incl id/next preservation and CLEAR omitting SET-only fields, not just rendering. No disabled/skipped tests counted as coverage (no @Disabled in any cited file). The engine IT seeds NON-default booleans precisely to defeat a null-fallback-defaults builder. The dispatch IT asserts exactly-one execution + identity + depth (a misconfigured seed would be zero) rather than a bare 'something happened'.

pyramid_verdict.balance: Correct and as designed. Unit-heavy base: copyOf (FunnelStepTest), executor branch logic + markup builders + error mapping + trim/PII (FunnelStepExecutorTest, all collaborators mocked, no over-mock since the renderer is a real static util), and the frontend form/preview Vitest specs. Validation is double-covered: backend (FunnelServiceKeyboardStepTest, default-lane persist round-trip) + frontend mirror (FunnelStepForm.keyboard) — justified because client and server validators are independent code paths that must agree byte-for-byte (Decision 6). The slow-lane @Tag('slow') ITs (FunnelExecutionEngineIT) are correctly limited to the cross-component invariants that cannot be proven on mocks: the exact /sendMessage wire body, completed-not-parked, and the keyword-dispatch leg. Controller-IT (default lane) carries the HTTP round-trip + preview. E2E correctly None per user-spec (reply keyboards render only in a real Telegram client; manual leg is smoke.md / Task 7). No pyramid inversion; no redundant duplication that reduces zero confidence. The one classification nuance (FunnelServiceKeyboardStepTest is an IT covering unit-level validation logic) is acceptable — see F-INFO-1.
